panels.description: 5xx error rate across all three services. Any sustained non-zero value is worth investigating immediately.
panels.title: HTTP 5xx error rate

panels.description: All HTTP responses per minute across all services, stacked by status code, so overall traffic volume and its composition (2xx/4xx/5xx) are visible together - not just errors.
panels.title: HTTP Request Throughput by Application & Status (1m)

panels.description: p95 HTTP server latency per service, from Micrometer's auto-instrumented http_server_requests_seconds histogram.
panels.title: HTTP p95 latency
Decline rate by reason over time
Fraud check latency (as observed by auth-service)

panels.description: Live state of the fraudService circuit breaker. Green=closed (healthy), yellow=half_open (probing recovery), red=open (fast-failing).
panels.title: Circuit state (fraudService)

panels.description: Why the circuit tripped: failed calls accumulate before the trip, then not_permitted (fast-fail rejections) take over once it's open.
panels.title: Circuit breaker call outcomes (fraudService)

panels.description: Fraud check outcomes as returned by fraud-service to callers: approve/decline/duplicate/conflict/in_progress/error. 'duplicate' is a replayed decision from an earlier identical request, not a fresh evaluation.
panels.title: Fraud decisions/min by outcome

panels.description: Server-side (fraud-service) fraud check latency by outcome. Compare against the client-side latency panel to spot circuit-breaker/network overhead.
panels.title: Fraud check latency by outcome (server-side p95)

panels.description: Time between outbox event creation and successful publish to Kafka.
panels.title: Outbox publish lag

panels.description: Number of outbox events not yet successfully published (status NEW or PUBLISHING).
panels.title: Outbox backlog

panels.description: Outbox publish attempt outcomes. A non-zero 'failed' rate means events exhausted retries and are stuck (status FAILED); a persistent 'retry' rate without a matching rise in 'success' suggests a downstream/broker problem.
panels.title: Outbox publish attempts/min by result

panels.description: Compares the rate of records received by the ledger consumer against the raw Kafka consumer group lag. A widening gap indicates the consumer is stuck or falling behind.
panels.title: Consumer throughput per min vs. lag (auth.events)

panels.description: Events successfully routed through LedgerEventProcessor by event type and outcome (success/ignored/error). 'success' includes duplicate deliveries safely skipped - see the duplicate-skipped panel below for that breakdown.
panels.title: Ledger events processed/min by type and result

panels.description: Events skipped because they were already processed (duplicate Kafka delivery caught by the processed_event idempotency guard). A small non-zero rate here is expected/healthy evidence the dedup safeguard is working, not a failure signal by itself.
panels.title: Ledger duplicate events skipped/min by type

panels.description: Rate of Kafka records published to the ledger dead-letter topic, broken down by the exception that caused recovery. Any sustained non-zero value indicates permanently failing records that require investigation.
panels.title: DLT publishes/min by topic and exception

panels.description: Idempotency cache (Redis) lookup outcomes. A rising error rate indicates Redis degradation, silently failing open to the normal DB path.
panels.title: Idempotency cache outcomes per minute

panels.description: Percentage of idempotency lookups served from Redis cache (hit) rather than falling through to the DB pre-check/transactional path.
panels.title: Idempotency cache hit rate
